messages:
lucy (People Ops): Quick post-all-hands thread to catch remaining Qs: reviews, leveling, promotions, comp, benefits, and appeals. Keep replies short; we'll route to owners. Key dates: calibration window 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-14, manager confirmations due 2025-11-10, retro pay target 2025-12-01.

dan (IC): If my manager recommends no level change but I have clear impact examples, what's the best way to surface them? Can peers submit directly?

maya (Eng Manager): Peers can add written evidence to the peer-evidence doc; ask your manager to include it in the calibration packet. If manager disagrees and you still have new evidence after calibration, there's a formal appeals window.

dan (IC): How long is the appeals window and who reviews it?

lucy (People Ops): Appeals open after final calibration sign-off and last for 10 business days. Appeals are reviewed by People Ops + a cross-functional appeal reviewer (manager peer + HR). We'll publish the exact dates after sign-off.

rahul (Recruiter): Hiring question: for candidates who start mid-cycle, can managers request an early leveling review? We've got two PMs starting 2 weeks before snapshot.

lucy (People Ops): Mid-cycle hires: rule of thumb is evaluate at next cycle unless they start >30 days before snapshot. Managers can submit an exception with strong rationale (business impact + artifacts); those are decided case-by-case.

erin (CFO): A note on comp: market adjustments are still processed via the comp-case flow. If you see broad pattern skews, escalate to People Ops + Finance.

payroll-bot: FYI: retro pay for promotions approved this cycle is scheduled for 2025-12-01 payroll. Payroll will DM individuals if there are discrepancies.

dan (IC): Out-of-cycle promotions  if approved, do they get retro pay too?

lucy (People Ops): Out-of-cycle promos may get retro pay depending on approval timing and payroll cutoff; People Ops will confirm on a case-by-case basis. Managers must submit comp-change forms for out-of-cycle cases.

dan (IC): Will there be an artifact checklist for managers? Some of our team leads asked for examples they can copy.

maya (Eng Manager): We standardized on 2 impact bullets + 1 artifact (PR, metric, customer quote). Short, outcome-focused bullets work best.

lucy (People Ops): I'll post a one-page artifact checklist and a short FAQ (timelines + appeals steps) in #announcements and the handbook by EOD tomorrow.

peopleops-bot: Resources pinned -> /handbook/reviews/calibration-rubric and /forms/appeals-request.

erin (CFO): Leadership ask: please ensure managers block 1.5 hours for calibration reviews; it materially improves fairness.

dan (IC): One last thing: can People Ops share anonymized examples of strong evidence (redacted) so ICs know what to include?

lucy (People Ops): Yes  we'll redact and publish 3 anonymized examples in the handbook along with the artifacts checklist. If you want to submit an internal example for redaction, DM me.

lucy (People Ops): Thanks all  if you have edge cases DM People Ops or reply here. We'll keep this thread for quick clarifications only.
